provenance.notes: Built from the 2012 base-game rulebook's bundled Scenario Book (reference/extracted/MK_base_rulebook_2012.txt, PDF p.12-19), cross-checked with the UE rulebook's scenario summaries (MKUE Rulebook p.14-22). The UE Scenario Book is a separate booklet that is NOT in our sources, so expansion scenarios (Volkare's Quest / Volkare's Return, Lost Legion and Shades of Tezla scenarios) are missing. Where the two printings differ (e.g. spell card numbers: 2012 = 17-20, UE = 109-112) the caveat records both. 'first-conquest' is a deliberate Emberwold variant from docs/design/11-mvp-scope.md, not an official scenario.
provenance.official_cross_check: Solo Conquest parameters agree in MKUE Rulebook p.19 and MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17: wedge, 7 countryside, 2 city + 2 non-city core tiles, cities level 5 then 8, six rounds, dummy player, four competitive Spells removed, one interactive Skill removed.

sources: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.12-19 (scenario book; full text)
MKUE Rulebook p.14-22 (scenario summaries, solo/coop rules)

items.name: Blitz Conquest
special_rules: start with 1 Fame; whenever you cross a Fame line gain 1 extra Fame
start with +2 Reputation
one extra Source die and one extra Unit in the offer
items.end_condition: When all cities are conquered every player has one last turn; if the Round ends during this the game ends immediately.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.16; MKUE Rulebook p.19
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: Blitz Cooperation

removals.detail: remove the four competitive Spells and one interactive Skill per player

special_rules: start with 1 Fame; crossing a Fame line gives 1 extra Fame
start with +2 Reputation
one extra Source die and one extra Unit in the offer
Full Cooperation rules apply with the shorter map
items.end_condition: When all cities are conquered every player except the Dummy player has one last turn.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17; MKUE Rulebook p.20
items.caveat: Cooperative scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: Classic (official Solo Conquest shape)

map.layout_note: Tile deck per standard rules: wedge map, starting tile A; core city/non-city tiles chosen as the scenario specifies (MKUE Rulebook p.3).

removals.detail: Remove the four competitive Spells and the one interactive Skill. 2012 numbering: Spells 17-20 (Mana Meltdown, Mana Claim, Mind Read, Energy Flow). UE numbering: Spells 109-112.

special_rules: when taking Tactics you always choose first; the Dummy player then takes one random card from the remaining
at the end of each Day or Night remove both used Tactic cards from the game (each Tactic is picked once)
Dummy player uses a standard 16-card hero deck with three starting crystals
items.end_condition: When all cities are conquered you have one last turn (the Dummy player does not).
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17 (SOLO CONQUEST); MKUE Rulebook p.19
items.caveat: Official Solo Conquest shape from the 2012 printing. The UE Scenario Book itself is unavailable; values were cross-checked against the UE rulebook summary p.19 and agree. Spell card numbering differs between printings (17-20 vs 109-112).

items.name: Conquer and Hold
items.rounds_note: 4 rounds with 4 players; 6 rounds in a 2-player game (MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.19)

map.layout_note: Predefined map: B side of the starting tile, three revealed countryside tiles, plus predefined positions for 2 more countryside and 4 core tiles. The picture is in the 2012 rulebook and not extracted as text, so the exact layout is not encoded.

cities.note: white city; friendly but closes its gates, cannot be entered

removals.detail: remove level IV Units (city-only recruitable) from the Elite Unit deck

special_rules: regular Units only in the first half; both regular and elite in the second half (from Round 3 in 4p / Round 4 in 3p)
monastery units also recruitable at mage towers; village units also recruitable at keeps
no reputation loss for assaulting keeps/mage towers
mage towers work like keeps in this scenario and give mana when you start in/next to one you control
2 player game: draw two gray/violet tokens when attacking a keep/tower; three during the third Day/Night
items.end_condition: Played until the round limit, or until one side admits the other has won.

scoring.note: 25 victory points available in total; a tie means nobody wins.

items.caveat: Team/competitive scenario from the 2012 scenario book; out of Emberwold v1 scope. The predefined map layout is a picture and is not encoded.

items.name: Druid Nights

map.layout_note: Remove tiles with no magical glades; core city is always the green city.

special_rules: mark magical glades with shields; incantation summons one brown enemy per marked glade during the first Night and red enemies during the second Night
defeated summoned enemies give double Fame
city is friendly, no leader
items.end_condition: When all players have performed the incantation during the second Night (each gets one more turn), or at the end of the second Night.
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: Dungeon Lords

map.layout_note: Remove tiles with no dungeons; core city is always the blue city; always include the desert tile with monastery and tomb.

special_rules: secret dungeon entrances are placed next to revealed villages
secret tombs are placed next to revealed monasteries
all conquered dungeons/tombs are connected for movement (2 Move + 1 per space)
city is friendly, no leader
items.end_condition: When all tiles are revealed and all dungeons and tombs are conquered every player has one last turn.
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: First Conquest

map.layout_note: Fixed hand-authored placement is a Emberwold design decision, not an official layout. TODO: author explicit hex-adjacency placement (start tile A centre; 2 countryside tiles on the wedge frontier; 1 city tile at the far end) plus site seeding (village, monastery, keep, mage tower, magical glade, crystal mine, rampaging orcs) in a follow-up data pass.

items.dummy_player_note: Simplified Emberwold dummy: consumes tactics and provides round-clock pressure (see docs/design/11-mvp-scope.md); full official dummy logic lives in the Classic preset.

removals.detail: Remove the four competitive Spells and the non-matching interactive Skill, as in official Solo Conquest (MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17).

special_rules: Emberwold tuned variant; not an official scenario
target session length 20-30 minutes; target win rate roughly 50%
tuned scoring weights (see scoring.tuning)

tactics.note: same tactic rules as Solo Conquest (MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17)

items.end_condition: The game ends when the single city is conquered (after the conquering turn); a round limit of 3 also ends it as a loss if the city still stands.

tuning.note: Weights to be tuned in playtest; structure mirrors official Solo Conquest scoring for easy A/B comparison.

items.official_ref: docs/design/11-mvp-scope.md §4.1; shape derived from official Solo Conquest (MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17 / MKUE Rulebook p.19)
items.caveat: Emberwold-specific variant. Tile/site layout and tuned scoring are design decisions and are not authored yet (layout_status=todo).

items.name: First Reconnaissance

map.layout_note: countryside tiles sorted by number for the first game (MKUE Walkthrough p.2)

removals.detail: For the first game use only Advanced Action cards 65-80 (2012/UE numbering) and do not reveal Spells/AAs until needed.

special_rules: a player scores 1 Fame whenever a new tile is revealed
no player-vs-player combat unless agreed
cities cannot be conquered or entered
guarantee at least one village-recruitable Unit in the initial offer
solo variant: 8 countryside tiles, 4 rounds (2 day, 2 night), dummy player, no titles
items.end_condition: When a player reveals a city tile, everyone has one last turn; if the Round ends during this, the game ends immediately.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.15; MKUE Rulebook p.18; MKUE Walkthrough p.1-4
items.caveat: Base-game/solo-variant setup data; not needed for Emberwold v1.

items.name: Full Conquest

map.layout_note: Wedge uses starting tile A; fully-open uses starting tile B (MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.12).

removals.detail: competitive scenario, keep all cards and skills

special_rules: standard game; cities all level 4
items.end_condition: When all cities are conquered every player has one last turn; if the Round ends during this the game ends immediately.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.16; MKUE Rulebook p.19
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: Full Cooperation

removals.detail: remove the four competitive Spells and one interactive Skill per player

special_rules: Dummy player takes a random Tactic first, then players choose
at the end of each Day/Night remove one Tactic used by a player
team rules apply (one shared score)
items.end_condition: When all cities are conquered every player except the Dummy player has one last turn.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.16; MKUE Rulebook p.20
items.caveat: Cooperative scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope (solo only).

items.name: Mines Liberation

map.layout_note: Remove tiles with no mines; core city is always the red city.

special_rules: mines are guarded and must be liberated; liberated mines produce crystals at the start of each Day/Night
city is friendly; each player puts a shield on it but no leader exists
items.end_condition: When all tiles are revealed and all mines liberated every player has one last turn.
items.official_ref: MK Base Rulebook 2012 p.17; MKUE Rulebook p.20
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.

items.name: One to Return
special_rules: portal closes at the end of Day 1; afterwards it is an empty plain space
no scoring; the hero on the portal at the end of the second Night wins
items.end_condition: The scenario ends as soon as the second Night is over; the hero standing on the portal wins.
items.caveat: Competitive scenario; out of Emberwold v1 scope.
